hook.line: Sometimes people see exactly what is going on and decide not to. *Hacer la vista gorda* names that choice, and you will hear it whenever someone talks about the authorities.
hook.es: Las autoridades hicieron la vista gorda ante los abusos.
hook.en: The authorities turned a blind eye to the abuses.

examples.es: Las autoridades hicieron la vista gorda ante los abusos.
examples.en: The authorities turned a blind eye to the abuses.
She preferred to look the other way.

examples.es: La policía hizo la vista gorda ante el ruido.
examples.en: The police turned a blind eye to the noise.

examples.es: No puedo hacer la vista gorda con esto.
examples.en: I can't turn a blind eye to this.
Why did you turn a blind eye?

examples.es: Don Hernando no hace la vista gorda con nadie.
examples.en: Don Hernando turns a blind eye to no one.

rule:
*Hacer la vista gorda* means to see something wrong and pretend you did not. It is a choice, never a lack of sight.

Only *hacer* changes: *hago*, *hizo*, *hicieron*, *hacer*. The rest stays: *la vista gorda*, always *la*, always singular.

To say what you ignore, use *ante* or *con*: *ante los abusos*, *con esto*.

A second way to say it: *mirar para otro lado*, to look the other way.
smallPrint: Teachers call this an idiom: you cannot work out the meaning from the words, so you learn it whole.

readAndPick.es: La policía hizo la vista gorda ante el ruido.
options: The police turned a blind eye to the noise.
The police never heard the noise.
The police complained about the noise.

readAndPick.es: No puedo hacer la vista gorda con esto.
options: I can't see this properly.
I can't turn a blind eye to this.
I won't be able to do this.
She preferred to talk to someone else.
She preferred to look at the problem.
She preferred to look the other way.

readAndPick.es: Las autoridades hicieron la vista gorda ante los abusos.
options: The authorities turned a blind eye to the abuses.
The authorities stopped the abuses.
The authorities will turn a blind eye to the abuses.
Why will you turn a blind eye?
Why did he turn a blind eye?
Why did you turn a blind eye?

readAndPick.es: Don Hernando no hace la vista gorda con nadie.
options: Don Hernando turns a blind eye to everyone.
Don Hernando turns a blind eye to no one.
Don Hernando can't see anyone.

readAndPick.es: El alcalde hizo la vista gorda.
options: The mayor turned a blind eye.
The mayor can't see well.
The mayor will turn a blind eye.

readAndPick.es: Muchos hacen la vista gorda cuando les conviene.
options: Many people turn a blind eye when it suits them.
Many people never see a problem.
Many people turned a blind eye once.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *El alcalde hizo la ___ gorda.* (*vista* or *vistas*) The mayor turned a blind eye.
yourTurn.answer: El alcalde hizo la vista gorda.
yourTurn.why: The phrase is always *la vista gorda*, singular.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Las autoridades hicieron la vista gorda ___ los abusos.* (*ante* or *de*) The authorities turned a blind eye to the abuses.
yourTurn.answer: Las autoridades hicieron la vista gorda ante los abusos.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The police turned a blind eye to the noise.
yourTurn.answer: La policía hizo la vista gorda ante el ruido.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I can't turn a blind eye to this.
yourTurn.answer: No puedo hacer la vista gorda con esto.

yourTurn.prompt: Say to a friend: Why did you turn a blind eye?
yourTurn.why: *Hiciste* is the *tú* form of the past.

yourTurn.prompt: Change it to say they turned a blind eye: *El alcalde hizo la vista gorda.* (use *los alcaldes*)
yourTurn.answer: Los alcaldes hicieron la vista gorda.
yourTurn.why: A plural subject needs *hicieron*, but *la vista gorda* stays singular.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative, so that he lets nobody off: *Don Hernando hace la vista gorda con todos.*
yourTurn.answer: Don Hernando no hace la vista gorda con nadie.
yourTurn.why: With *no* in front of the verb, *todos* turns into *nadie*: Spanish keeps both negatives.

pitfalls.wrong: El alcalde hizo las vistas gordas.
pitfalls.right: El alcalde hizo la vista gorda.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The phrase is fixed: *la vista gorda*, never plural.

pitfalls.wrong: Las autoridades hicieron la vista gorda de los abusos.
pitfalls.right: Las autoridades hicieron la vista gorda ante los abusos.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "to", but Spanish uses *ante* (or *con*) here.

pitfalls.wrong: El alcalde hizo el ojo ciego.
pitfalls.right: El alcalde hizo la vista gorda.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "blind eye", but Spanish says "fat sight": *la vista gorda*.

personal: Think of a time someone saw something and said nothing. Say it: *… hizo la vista gorda…*.
